text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime minister to Palestinians: Don't lose faith.
- Israeli army prepared, hopes for quiet weekend.
- Table tennis coach convicted of spying for Russia.
- El-Rov may put Jerusalem hotel construction on hold due to tourism crisis.
- Koor president Benjamin Gaon seeks CEOs' meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
GLOBES
- Growing fears of financial buckling by the Histadrut within a few months.
HAARETZ

- At Erez crossing talks between Israel and Palestinians there will be a discussion of administering partition areas between cities of the West Bank and Israeli army forces. Israel demands Palestinian Authority improve supervision over weapons use and arm police at sensitive posts -- such as Hebron and Joseph's Tomb -- with pistols rather than rifles.
- Israel rejects Palestinian demand for security control of any kind in Gaza airport, will at Erez propose two models.
MAARIV
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: We were nearly in the abyss -- don't lose hope.
- Author Amos Oz: Let's go to the final-status talks.
- U.S. army chief cancels visit to Israel. Military source says it's only a postponement and has nothing to do with recent events.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Series of gestures to Palestinians ahead of talks in Erez such as pulling tanks back from cities in the West Bank and easing the closure.

- Expert on pressure situations: Most of the public in fear. Poll shows 79 percent of the Israeli public worried about the security situation of Israel. Did the summit succeed? 46 percent say yes, 48 percent no.
